subject: Clarify: SOC 2 scope for EU-hosted deployment — bridge letter & audit window
messages:
From: Sophie Larsson <sophie.larsson@finreg.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: DPO Contact <dpo@finreg.com>
Date: 2026-02-08T08:14:00Z
Subject: SOC 2 scope and hosting jurisdiction — immediate ask

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — FinReg is moving quickly on the PoC and we need to close a couple of compliance checks before procurement can sign off. Two quick questions:  

1) For Redwood Private deployed into our EU VPC (we plan to use eu-west-1), does your SOC 2 Type II report explicitly cover controls for the EU-hosted deployment, or is the report scoped to Redwood’s control plane only? We need to know whether the audit period and scope cover the actual data residency for the timeframe Jan 1 2025 — Dec 31 2025.

2) If the report does not explicitly state EU-hosted coverage, can Redwood provide a bridge letter (or attestation) that confirms:
   - the audit period covered the controls relevant to hosting/processing;
   - any cross-border replication/backups during that window and the dates of any topology changes (e.g., when EU-only hosting began); and
   - whether customer data for FinReg would have remained within EU boundaries if we had an EU-dedicated deployment?

Procurement would like either a statement we can attach to the SOC 2 or a short bridge letter we can include with our internal risk register.

Appreciate a quick take — we’re targeting a procurement review next week.

Best,
Sophie
Senior Compliance Manager
FinReg Solutions

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-08T11:02:00Z
Subject: Fwd: SOC 2 scope and hosting jurisdiction — FinReg request (need bridge letter draft)

Connor / Marissa — forwarding FinReg's request (below). They want to know whether our SOC 2 Type II covers EU-hosted deployments for the Jan–Dec 2025 audit window and are asking for either a clarifying statement or a bridge letter.

Key asks they need addressed:
- Confirm whether the SOC 2 report (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_20250131.pdf) includes control coverage for EU-hosted Private deployments in eu-west-1 during 2025, or if there were topology/backups that created cross-border transfers.
- If full coverage isn't in the report language, can Security/Legal produce a short bridge letter that states the effective dates of EU-residency for customer data and any exceptions (e.g., replication windows, support access from US operators) so Sophie can attach it to her risk register.

I've attached the SOC 2 we typically share and a blank bridge letter template. Can one of you draft a 1-page attestation we can send to Sophie by EOD tomorrow? If there are limitations we should call them out explicitly (e.g., control plane located in US but data plane in EU; backups replicated until X date).

Also tagging Marissa for legal sign-off language and to confirm phrasing around "no intentional cross-border processing after [date]".

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-08T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: SOC 2 scope and hosting jurisdiction — FinReg request (need bridge letter draft)

Vanessa / Marissa,

Quick summary from Security ops after reviewing the 2025 SOC 2 artifacts:  

- The issued SOC 2 Type II (period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31) covers Redwood's control environment for our managed hosted services and for our Dedicated offering when running in our verified partner regions. The report's language references controls over the "service organization infrastructure and supporting systems" but does not enumerate every customer VPC location by region.

- For Private deployments where the customer requests an EU-only data plane, Redwood supported an EU-dedicated deployment model in eu-west-1 starting 2025-03-01. Prior to that date some backups/replication for newly provisioned accounts were routed to a manged replication bucket in us-west-2 for resilience during onboarding (this was documented as part of our provisioning playbook).

- Implication: the SOC 2 Type II controls apply to the functions and processes used to operate both the control plane and the data plane. However, the report's descriptive section does not explicitly state "EU-residency for all customer data for the full audit period." For procurement purposes, a bridge letter that calls out the operational facts (dates and any replication windows) plus confirmation of encryption at rest and access controls should be acceptable.

Actionable suggestion for the bridge letter content (draft bullets):
- Statement of audit period covered (2025-01-01 — 2025-12-31) and the SOC 2 opinion issued 2026-01-31.
- Statement that Redwood supported EU-only data plane deployments in eu-west-1 beginning 2025-03-01.
- Note that for newly provisioned accounts between 2025-01-01 and 2025-02-28, limited cross-region backup replication to us-west-2 occurred; after 2025-03-01, customer data for EU-dedicated deployments remained within eu-west-1 for primary storage and operational processing.
- Confirmation of encryption at rest (AES-256) and customer-key options (KMS) for Private deployments.
- Standard caveat: bridge letters are attestations of operational facts and do not replace an audit; include contact for follow-up.

Marissa — can you review and convert to legal-safe language? I can mark up the draft.

Connor
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-08T16:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: SOC 2 scope and hosting jurisdiction — FinReg request (need bridge letter draft)

Thanks — I reviewed Connor's suggested bullets and edited for procurement-safe phrasing. See attached draft (draft_bridge_letter_finreg_20260208.docx). Key legal refinements:

- Replaced "remained within eu-west-1" with "processed and stored in eu-west-1 for primary operational workloads" to avoid implying absolute restrictions on transient backups unless we can certify them.
- Added a line clarifying that the SOC 2 report addresses Redwood's control environment and operating procedures applicable to the service as implemented during the audit period; it does not constitute an audit of any single customer's specific VPC configuration.
- Included a point about support/maintenance access: engineers may access logs or troubleshooting artifacts from our support environment when explicitly authorized by the customer under existing contractual terms.

I propose we send Sophie: the SOC 2 PDF, the attached draft bridge letter signed by Legal, and a short note summarizing the dates and the replication exception window (2025-01-01 to 2025-02-28). Vanessa — shall I sign the bridge letter or do you want Legal to send from the Legal mailbox?

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
